column1: # trusted-type-error-causes.tsv — the MEASURED first Why3 error, at FULL WIDTH, on a PRISTINE
# tree, for every `\trusted` marker whose conversion lowers to a TYPE ERROR. One row per marker.
# THIS FILE TOOK THREE MEASUREMENTS TO GET RIGHT, and the two failures are both truncations of a
# different kind. They are recorded here because the numbers below are only as good as the
# instrument, and the instrument was wrong twice in one hour.
#   1. THE SCREEN that produced the original "230 type errors" table cut each Why3 message at 48
#      characters, so it could only group by the type the emitter EXPECTED. A 174-witness wall was
#      sized from that grouping and the capability built against it cleared ONE of 103.
#   2. THE FIRST RE-MEASUREMENT captured ONE line per message. A Why3 type error is TWO lines —
#      `has type X,` then `but is expected to have type Y` — so half of every row was the half
#      that distinguishes a cause from a symptom.
#   3. THE SECOND RE-MEASUREMENT restored a pristine copy of the FILE it was about to edit and
#      left the PREVIOUS file converted. Once the candidate list crossed a file boundary, every
#      later candidate was measured against a mirror in which earlier files were still converted.
#      MEASURED: with NO port at all (the porter ABORTED), the contaminated tree still printed
#      `list.List.list PyCSL_Program.pyval, but is expected to have type int` for `pycsl.py`,
#      which imports Module5_IREmitter and Module6_WhyMLTranspiler. THIRTEEN of 116 rows changed
#      when the whole mirror was restored per candidate. See wall-lessons.md (t6).
# THE ROWS BELOW ARE THE THIRD MEASUREMENT: per candidate, `git archive HEAD src/self-annotate/src`
# extracted fresh over the mirror, the marker ported (or `--replace`d) and deleted, the file
# emitted, the first Why3 error flattened to 220 characters. 115 of 116 produce a type error;
# ONE now LOWERS (`pure_ast.py::NodeVisitor.generic_visit`, which the four conversion oracles then
# 102 of the 116 have exactly ONE side `int`: they fail at the SEAM between the faithful value
# model and the int-erased one. Those 102 are classified `cost-scale:int-erasure-seam` in
# `trusted-reasons.tsv` (backlog #62). The other 14 stay `unclassified` and are listed in #62.
